text: 📋 MAÑANERA BREAKDOWN — 31 de agosto de 2026. Resumen completo: presentaciones (El ABC de las emociones, encuesta docente sobre celulares, becas universales, recursos del caso García Luna para escuelas de La Montaña), preguntas y respuestas, y post potential.

🇲🇽📈 Tomorrow Sheinbaum delivers her Second Report. The numbers she brings: economy strong, homicides down, peso holding. "The Mexican economy is doing very well, despite the tariffs." — Claudia Sheinbaum, ahead of her Segundo Informe July inflation 3.12%; Q2 GDP +1.5%; daily homicides down 51%; the National Guard at 130,000 after seven years. The Informe is Sept 1 — no mañanera tomorrow.

🇲🇽🎨 The plan doesn't "fix" teachers — it trusts them. "This isn't about training teachers — they already have enormous experience." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 The emotional-health strategy gives teachers methodology and psychological backup rather than a script, working collectively with families and students. Teachers lead; the state supports.

🇲🇽✊ "Every girl has the right to be whatever she wants to be." "Equality and rights. Every girl has the right to be whatever she wants to be." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 Asked about gender messaging in the new school materials, Mexico's first woman president rejected the old stereotypes and grounded the curriculum in equality — any child can follow any path.

🇲🇽⚖️ 81% of Mexican teachers want phones out of the classroom — the government is listening to them, not the tech lobby. "81% of teachers agree that cellphones should not be used during class." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 The stance came with a pointed reference to litigation showing Meta deliberately engineered addictive design. A survey of 565,396 teachers found 48% say phones erode classroom attention; national guidelines will be set with every state's education secretary.

🇲🇽✊ "We don't want anyone to leave school for economic reasons." "Everyone has talent, everyone should be recognized — we don't want anyone dropping out over money." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 Sheinbaum defended universal scholarships over merit-based aid: the Rita Cetina scholarship now reaches nearly 10 million students. A child who didn't arrive fed, she said, won't learn the same — so support is a right, not a prize.

🇲🇽🎨 Mexico is putting emotional health on the school schedule — one hour a week, nationwide. "We will all support adolescents growing up in a healthy way, so they always have a friend in their teacher and in their classmates." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 "El ABC de las emociones" launches with 16 million guides for students, teachers and families: weekly sessions on mental health, emotional literacy and safe social-media use, backed by the Línea de la Vida (800-911-2000).

🔥🇲🇽 The money García Luna stole is going to build schools in Mexico's poorest mountains. "Our goal is for this money to go to schools in La Montaña de Guerrero — for the areas of greatest need in the country." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 $5.8 million recovered from the Weinberg family — tied to jailed ex-security chief Genaro García Luna — reached Mexico's treasury Aug 25, from a forfeited bond and 12 liquidated Florida properties. It now funds high schools and universities in La Montaña de Guerrero.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>The World Cup left Mexico $2.5 billion</u>

The 2026 World Cup delivered Mexico a $2,543-million-dollar economic impact — 0.12% of GDP and 101,255 temporary jobs — with gastronomy alone adding $584M in sales and Mexico City leading at $548M, per Deloitte's study reported by El Economista. Tourism Secretary Josefina Rodríguez, to the doubters: "It did have an impact; our job now is to turn it into permanent benefits."
